href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-wkitlkk-l-iy/" target="_blank" >55th annual Chicago Pride Parade marches on despite attacks against community</a></h3><p></p><h5>By <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-wkitlkk-l-ij/" target="_blank" >Violet Miller</a></h5><p>The 55th annual Chicago Pride Parade strutted Sunday in Lake View, bringing thousands to the 20-block route. With 155 entrants, it was four parade floats longer than last year's.</p><p>This year’s theme, "Free to Be Proud," comes amid increasing attacks on LGBTQ+ communities across the nation — including in Illinois, which is largely considered <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-wkitlkk-l-it/" target="_blank" >a haven for queer people</a> in the Midwest.</p><p>Miley Asari, a born and raised Roscoe Village resident, has been to the parade enough times that she knew to quickly find a shady spot on the route.</p><p>Along the way, she spotted lots of queer youth, which she said is a testament to the progress being made and "how far we’ve come." To her, "this is Chicago."</p><p>Friends Olivia Atkins and Kalyah Jackson’s drive from Bloomington in Central Illinois took almost as long as it took Atkins to make the crocheted lesbian flag-inspired hats they wore there.</p><p>Jackson said she loves the outfits that surround her every year at the event — this being her fourth — but more than anything, she takes comfort in being in community.</p><p>"I just enjoy being around my people," Jackson said. "Love whoever you want, and even though there's people who don’t think that way, it's nice to know you’re surrounded by people who do."</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-wkitlkk-l-ii/" target="_blank" ><b>READ MORE</b></a></p><hr><p></p><h4>YOUR DAILY QUESTION ☕️</h4><p><b>Calling all experienced boaters: What practical tips do you have for a first-time boater in the Chicago area?</b></p><p><a class="Link" href="mailto:newsletters@suntimes.com" target="_blank" ><i>Respond via email </i></a><i>(please include your first and last name). We may run your answer in a future newsletter or story.</i></p><hr><p>Thanks for reading the Sun-Times Morning Edition!<br>Got a story you think we missed? <a class="Link" href="mailto:newsletters@suntimes.com" target="_blank" >Email us here.</a></p><hr><p><b>Written and curated by</b>: Matt Moore<br><b>Editor</b>: Eydie Cubarrubia</p><hr><p><i>The Chicago Sun-Times is a nonprofit supported by readers like you. Become a member to make stories like these free and available to everyone. Learn more at </i><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-wkitlkk-l-ih/" target="_blank" ><i>suntimes.com/member</i></a><i>.</i></p>

entries.title: Everything Cubs, White Sox and baseball fans need to know about NBC's 'Star-Spangled Sunday'
entries.summary: <p>Cubs and White Sox fans — and most baseball fans, for that matter — will need Peacock to watch their teams play Sunday, when NBCUniversal presents all 15 MLB games on the schedule, a first for a media company in a single day.</p><p>NBCU’s “Star-Spangled Sunday” includes two games on NBC and three on NBC Sports Network that will simulcast on Peacock. Every other game will be exclusive to Peacock, including the Sox-Guardians game at 1 p.m. and Cardinals-Cubs at 1:30.</p><p>Each game will have a dedicated broadcast crew, some of which will be a combination of announcers from the participating teams. Guardians play-by-play voice Matt Underwood will join Sox analyst Steve Stone in the booth, with Guardians reporter Andre Knott on the field. The Cubs game will have an all-Cubs crew of Alex Cohen, Mark Sweeney and Taylor McGregor.</p><p>“There is no home base studio show on the day, but there will be consistency throughout all these presentations in the graphics look,” said Rob Hyland, NBC Sports’ senior vice president of production and coordinating producer, who will oversee “Star-Spangled Sunday.”</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: Los bates de los Sox se vuelven locos con 22 carreras en la apertura de la serie: ‘Fue una noche especial’
entries.summary: <p>Miguel Vargas inició el ataque con un batazo hacia el bullpen del jardín izquierdo, y después de eso los White Sox nunca se detuvieron.</p><p>Para cuando terminaron, igualaron la segunda mayor cantidad de carreras en la historia de la franquicia. Fue una noche de ese tipo para ellos.</p><p>Vargas y Jacob González jonronearon en una tercera entrada de 10 carreras, y los Sox aplastaron a los Royals 22-1 el viernes.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-f60000" name="module-f60000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Los Sox conectaron cinco jonrones en su partido con mayor cantidad de carreras desde que anotaron 22 en Boston el 31 de mayo de 1970. El récord de la franquicia es de 29 carreras contra los Kansas City Athletics el 23 de abril de 1955.</p><p>Tristan Peters conectó su primer cuadrangular con las bases llenas e impulsó seis carreras. Andrew Benintendi y Kyle Teel también jonronearon.</p><p>Chase Meidroth tuvo cuatro de los 23 hits más altos de la temporada para los Sox y anotó tres carreras. Vargas y González cada uno tuvo tres hits y cinco carreras impulsadas.</p><p>“Es increíble”, dijo Peters.</p><p>“Es muy divertido cuando todos están bien, ven la pelota bien y todos quieren batear”.</p><p>Los Sox (42-38) pasaron un juego por delante de Cleveland (42-40) en la lucha por el liderato de la División Central de la Liga Americana, con los Guardians perdiendo ante los Mariners. También mejoraron a 27-13 en el Rate Field. Solo los Rays tienen un mejor récord en casa con 29-12.</p><p>“Fue especial, fue una noche especial”, dijo el manager Will Venable. “Cosas realmente buenas en toda la alineación. Todos contribuyeron; los chicos de la banca hicieron un buen trabajo. Tan buena como fue nuestra ofensiva, pensé que nuestro pitcheo también fue genial”.</p><p>Los Sox rompieron el juego en la tercera entrada, enviando a 14 bateadores al plato. Para cuando terminaron, lograron su entrada con más carreras desde una segunda entrada de 11 carreras en Cincinnati el 7 de mayo de 2023.</p><p>Vargas inició el festín con su jonrón número 18, un batazo de tres carreras hacia el jardín izquierdo contra Mitch Spence (0-2) después de que González recibiera base por bolas con un out y Sam Antonacci conectara un hit.</p><p>A partir de ahí, las cosas se salieron de control rápidamente.</p><p>Meidroth impulsó una carrera con un hit dentro del infield. Peters conectó un hit que trajo dos más, y González siguió con un batazo de tres carreras hacia el jardín derecho. Vargas agregó un doble de RBI, colocando el marcador en 10-0, antes de que Teel se ponchara para finalizar el inning.</p><p>“Es como sentirse imparable, no paran”, dijo Peters. “Estamos como, wow, el que sigue. Todos esperan batear y conseguir un hit”.</p><p>Los Sox no se detuvieron ahí.</p><p>Benintendi hizo el 11-1 cuando abrió la cuarta entrada con su décimo jonrón, un batazo hacia el jardín derecho contra Beck Way. Teel agregó un jonrón de dos carreras en el quinto contra Lucas Erceg, siendo este su primer jonrón de la temporada.</p><p>Peters aumentó la ventaja a 17-1 en el sexto cuando envió un batazo al jardín derecho-central contra John Schreiber. El grand slam fue el sexto de los Sox esta temporada.</p><p>David Sandlin (2-1) permitió una carrera y tres hits en seis entradas tras ser llamado desde Triple-A Charlotte. Caminó a los primeros tres bateadores en la cuarta entrada antes de que Kansas City anotara su única carrera con un rodado que provocó un doble play de Michael Massey.</p><p>“Fue realmente genial ver a todos batear”, dijo González. “No solo eso, sino que los mantuvimos en una carrera. El pitcheo fue genial. Sandlin tuvo una entrada donde permitió una carrera, pero incluso entonces, lo superó, lo cual fue enorme. Simplemente un juego completo hoy”.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: Lions release cornerback Terrion Arnold days after arrest over kidmappings
entries.summary: <p>The Detroit Lions released cornerback Terrion Arnold on Monday, only days after his arrest over allegations that he orchestrated the abduction and beating of three men who prosecutors believe he wrongly suspected of having stolen luxury goods and $100,000 in cash from him.</p><p>The team made the announcement on the X social media platform. The Lions did not give a reason, but the announcement came the same day that a Florida judge set Arnold's bail at $1 million. Prosecutors say the three victims, including a man who worked as a driver for Arnold, were robbed while being held at gunpoint in a Tampa apartment in February.</p><p>Prosecutors had wanted Arnold held without bond on the eight felony charges he faces, but Chief Circuit Court Judge Christopher Sabella granted bond. He won't be required to wear an ankle monitor because it would prevent him from taking the field for games and training.</p><p>The judge said Arnold already has a "paparazzi monitor," referring to the photographers who have been watching his movements.</p><p>"If he shows up on a beach in Tahiti, he'll be on social media," Sabella said at the end of the bond hearing in Tampa.</p><p>Each charge could bring a life sentence if Arnold is convicted.</p><p>The judge did order Arnold to remain at his home in Tallahassee except for anything related to NFL training. He also said Arnold cannot have any contact with other people tied to the case and must surrender his passport within 48 hours.</p><p>Arnold, 23, was a first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after playing at Alabama. He had 31 tackles and an interception last season for Detroit. </p><p>According to prosecutors, the victims were abducted three days after cash and luxury items, including Rolex watches and Louis Vuitton bags, were reported stolen from Arnold at an Airbnb rental in the Tampa area. Prosecutors allege that six of Arnold's associates actually carried out the crimes, holding, beating and pistol-whipping the victims, and that Arnold wasn't there at the time.</p><p>None of Arnold's co-defendants had bond set for them. Two female co-defendants have pleaded guilty and are cooperating with authorities. Their statements tie Arnold, who was not at the apartment, to the crimes, according to prosecutors.</p>

entries.title: Sky Q&A: Will the return of DiJonai Carrington be able to turn this thing around?
entries.summary: <p>Thank you to everyone who wrote in about this head-scratcher of a Sky (6-13) season! Keep the questions coming. We'll do another one soon.</p><p><b>How does [general manager Jeff Pagliocca] justify his decision to sign 3 players [Azura Stevens, Courtney Vandersloot, DiJonai Carrington] who are/were injured such that they were not able to start the season? </b>-<b> </b><i>Doressia H</i></p><p>That’s the big question, isn’t it? The simplest way to put it is that Pagliocca and coach Tyler Marsh <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/05/22/sky-have-no-regrets-about-building-their-roster-around-injured-players" >really wanted these players in the program</a>, so much that they were willing to wait for them. They love Stevens as a floor spacer and think she has a ton of upside offensively. They love Vandersloot’s ability to run a team, and Carrington for all the things she’s known for.</p><p>The second piece of it though is that they believed the rest of the roster was strong enough to “hold it down” in their absence. Maybe that would have been true if they hadn’t lost Rickea Jackson to injury, or shot so poorly to start the season, or if Marsh had more experience — I’m really not sure. But they certainly weren’t expecting to be 5-12 when Vandersloot returned.</p><p><b>How do they recover from Rickea Jackson’s injury? [Jackson, the team’s leading scorer, tore her ACL in the fourth game of the season.] </b>-<b> </b><i>Twitter</i></p><p>I think the team is starting to discover a way forward. They’ve won two of their last three and are averaging 100+ points during that span. Everyone from the Wings’ Paige Bueckers to the Aces’ Jewell Loyd has told me that the Sky are far more dangerous than their record shows.</p><p>But it’s taken <i>a lot</i> of progress to get to this point. Stevens had to regain her confidence after a knee injury. Kamilla Cardoso had to find another gear. Sydney Taylor had to prove herself, and Marsh had to trust her with the starting slot.</p><p>If only they could’ve hammered some of these things out before sinking to the bottom of the standings! But, changes are bearing fruit: over the last eight games, the Sky are a top three offense in the league.</p><p><b>Will the return of DiJonai Carrington be able to turn this thing around? What’s the timeline for her return? </b>- <i>Kayla M.</i></p><p>To start with the positive: having a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/05/03/sky-defense-needs-dijonai-carrington-back-and-soon" >great wing defender like Carrington is a huge asset</a>. There are many great guards around the league —- think Rhyne Howard, Olivia Miles, Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark —- who require special attention and Carrington is just the player to give it to them.</p><p>The leadership piece will help too. Carrington is clearly a fountain of knowledge on defense, and the Sky want to define themselves on that side of the ball.</p><p>But I think what’s at the heart of your question is: the Sky have put themselves in a pretty big hole at 6-13, so it’s tough to see one player digging them out of it. That’s totally valid! Especially because Carrington will need time to settle in whenever she does return.</p><p>When exactly, will that be? What I can tell you is that she’s been doing individual workouts (meaning shooting, ball-handling, etc.) and rehab, but has not returned to practice. The team has <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/06/02/sky-injury-report-no-firm-timeline-for-dijonai-carrington-azura-stevens-still-finding-her-legs" >not given any sort of target date.</a></p><p><b>Why does the offense stray away from Kamilla Cardoso? </b><i>- Twitter</i></p><p>That was an early-season failure that the team recognizes and has gotten much better at. I think <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/06/28/sky-center-kamilla-cardoso-is-starting-to-play-like-an-all-star" >the last five games prove it</a>: Cardoso has been consistently involved, averaging 21.8 points on 75% shooting during that span.</p><p>Her avoiding foul trouble is key — when Marsh has to pull her out, it disrupts the flow and shortens her window of opportunity. Also, it does take more effort to get her involved than some of the better scorers in the league, many of whom you can just give the ball to on the perimeter and let go to work.</p><p><b>Is there a favorite song making its way through the team right now? </b>-<b> </b><i>Mike P.</i></p><p>I asked rookie forward Aicha Coulibaly about this and she couldn’t think of one. But she did say that she’s been singing “Say My Name” every day in the locker room, and veteran guard Rachel Banham is tired of it.</p>

entries.title: City officials warn residents, ramp up services for extreme heat hitting Chicago area
entries.summary: <p>City officials warned that sweltering temperatures gripping the Chicago area this week pose a significant risk to vulnerable communities, including older residents, people with disabilities, young children and those without access to air conditioning.</p><p>The National Weather Service has issued an extreme heat warning that will remain in effect through Wednesday evening. The heat index — which means what the hot air feels like when combined with humidity — will approach 105 degrees at times.</p><p>By 2:30 p.m. Monday, it was 90 degrees at O'Hare International Airport. Forecasters expected the high to reach 92 degrees.</p><p>"Extreme heat can be very dangerous," said Mayor Brandon Johnson during a morning press briefing at the city's Office of Emergency Management and Communications on the Near West Side. "This is the time to check in on our neighbors, especially elderly neighbors or those with disabilities or health challenges. Let's do what Chicagoans do best. Let's look out for one another."</p><p>NWS meteorologist Mike Bardou said during the briefing three-day stretches of heat like this week's "have only occurred twice since the beginning of 2013."</p><p>Bardou added that overnight temperatures were also an issue. Due to overnight temperatures remaining in the upper 70s and low 80s, residents are less likely to recover from daytime temperatures, he said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div aria-label="Next"> <svg class="FlickityCustomNavigation-button-icon"><use xlink:href="#icon-right"></use></svg> </button> </div> </div></div> </bsp-carousel> </div> </div><p>The risks prompted Johnson to invoke the historic 1995 heat wave. 793 Chicago residents died in the heat that year.</p><p>"Chicago knows perhaps better than any other city in America, the dangers of extreme weather and particularly heat," Johnson said. "From that tragedy, the City of Chicago learned how to be more proactive and responsive to our residents."</p><p>The weather service is not forecasting records to be broken, though temperatures may not be far from record levels, said Gino Izzi, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service.</p><p>And due to the possibility of thunderstorms, there may more of a range of temperatures on Thursday and Friday, Izzi said. "We just don't have a great view at this point."</p><p>Chicago last saw a similar stretch <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2025/06/22/heatwave-chicago-health-weather" target="_blank" >last summer</a>, when heat indices reached 100 or higher for four straight days from June 21 to June 24, Izzi said.</p><h3>Preparedness efforts</h3><p>The city's Department of Family and Support Services has activated six community service cooling centers and 20 senior centers all readily available until Thursday. The Garfield Community Service Center will remain open through Friday and will extend its hours until 8 p.m.</p><p>Residents will have access to 287 cooling facilities across the city, including Chicago Public Library branches, Park District facilities, City Colleges campuses and police district stations. Residents can locate the nearest cooling center by calling 311 or visiting the city's website.</p><p>DFSS Commissioner Angela Green said more than 31,000 robocalls were sent over the weekend to senior citizens offering wellness checks and reminding them of available resources. Street outreach teams will also be providing bottled water to the unhoused community, in addition to connecting them with shelters and cooling centers.</p><p>Department of Buildings Commissioner Marlene Hopkins said inspectors will enforce the city's cooling ordinance during the heat wave, ensuring qualifying residential buildings and care facilities have functioning air conditioning or accessible cooling areas.</p><p>Chicago Fire Commissioner Annette Nance-Holt said firefighters and paramedics are adding resources across the city while reminding residents never to leave children or pets inside parked vehicles, even for a few minutes. She also warned residents to avoid using illegal fireworks and to practice water safety during the upcoming Fourth of July holiday.</p><p>Residents are encouraged to drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol and caffeine, wear lightweight clothing and remain indoors whenever possible. Those without air conditioning should keep blinds closed while slightly opening windows for ventilation.</p><p>Officials stated anyone experiencing a medical emergency related to the heat should call 911 immediately, while non-emergency requests for cooling centers, wellness checks or other city services should be directed to 311.</p><p>ComEd said it has pre-staged additional crews and equipment across its territory and is monitoring conditions around the clock during the heat wave, ComEd spokesperson David Perez in a release.</p><p>Customers can report outages to ComEd by texting OUT to 26633, calling 1-800-EDISON-1, using the ComEd mobile app or visiting ComEd.com.</p><p>Chicago Public Schools said all summer programming would be held inside with air conditioning Monday through Wednesday under the district’s extreme heat policy.</p>

entries.title: ‘Cúpula de calor’ traerá temperaturas peligrosamente altas al área de Chicago esta semana
entries.summary: <p>La primera ola de calor del año en Chicago podría llegar en los próximos días, con temperaturas en aumento y un clima caluroso que probablemente se mantendrá durante la próxima semana y hasta el feriado del 4 de julio.</p><p>Se pronostican temperaturas "peligrosamente" altas en los 90 grados Fahrenheit, con índices de calor que podrían superar los 100 grados, desde el lunes hasta el viernes, según el Servicio Nacional de Meteorología (NWS).</p><p>Se anticipan las temperaturas más altas de lunes a miércoles, con condiciones calurosas y húmedas y poco o ningún alivio del Lago Michigan, informaron los funcionarios del clima. Es posible que haya tormentas el jueves y viernes, lo que podría traer algo de alivio, pero sin ellas, los índices de calor podrían alcanzar hasta 105 grados.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-710000" name="module-710000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Si la ola de calor se extiende hasta el 4 de julio dependerá de si se desarrollan tormentas que podrían enfriar la zona el próximo viernes, dijo el meteorólogo Zachary Yack del NWS.</p><p>"Si no hay tormentas, existe la posibilidad de que persista hasta el próximo fin de semana. Esa es la parte complicada y difícil de responder en este momento", comentó Yack.</p><p>Se espera que un alto nivel de presión atmosférica que ingresa al Medio Oeste y a la mitad este de EE.UU. "se mantenga estacionario" y cree lo que se denomina una "cúpula de calor" sobre la zona, explicó Yack.</p><p>"Cuando tienes eso, además del sol del verano, todo conduce a temperaturas calurosas, humedad y, por supuesto, esos índices de calor en niveles más preocupantes y peligrosos para aquellos que son sensibles al calor", agregó Yack.</p><p>Los funcionarios del NWS y de la Oficina de Manejo de Emergencias y Comunicaciones (OEMC) de Chicago instan a los residentes a comenzar a planificar con anticipación para el clima caluroso.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Aside from a few spotty showers well south of I-80, mainly dry conditions are expected early next week. The focus will turn to the hot and humid conditions developing with peak heat indices over 100 degrees for much of next week. <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/ILwx?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#ILwx</a> <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/INwx?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#INwx</a> <a href="https://t.co/89JRgT533G">pic.twitter.com/89JRgT533G</a></p>— NWS Chicago (@NWSChicago) <a href="https://x.com/NWSChicago/status/2070941323901731321?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">June 27, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>“Si vas a estar afuera la próxima semana, es mejor asegurarte de tener formas de mantenerte hidratado y fresco, como llevar contigo agua y bebidas frías”, dijo Yack. “Si eres alguien que trabaja al aire libre, asegúrate de planificar usar ropa más ligera. Planifica con anticipación”.</p><p>“Durante la ola de calor, verifica a tus vecinos, amigos, especialmente aquellos que tal vez tengan problemas médicos que el calor empeore”, comentó. “Si conoces a un amigo que no tiene aire acondicionado, contáctalo y asegúrate de que esté bien”.</p><p>El Departamento de Servicios Familiares y de Apoyo de la ciudad (DFSS) tiene planes de abrir los siguientes seis centros de enfriamiento de 9 a.m. a 5 p.m. de lunes a viernes:</p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-66c5dc50-73f9-11f1-a91d-173fd4d7b4fb"><li>Auburn Gresham Center, 1140 W. 79th St.</li><li>Garfield Center, 10 S. Kedzie Ave.</li><li>King Center, 4314 S. Cottage Grove</li><li>North Area Center, 845 W. Wilson Ave.</li><li>South Chicago Center, 8650 S. Commercial Ave.</li><li>Trina Dávila Center, 4312 W. North Ave.</li></ul><p>Los residentes también son bienvenidos a refrescarse en cualquiera de las ubicaciones de la Biblioteca Pública de Chicago (CPL), en los campos del Distrito de Parques de Chicago, en los campus principales de los City Colleges de Chicago (CCC) y en cualquiera de las 22 estaciones del Departamento de Policía de Chicago (CPD), donde también podrán conectarse con un refugio.</p><p>Se pueden solicitar chequeos de bienestar llamando al 311 o visitando <a class="Link" href="http://311.chicago.gov" target="_blank" >311.chicago.gov</a>.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (AI) y editado por </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a></p>

entries.title: Piping plover chicks named after 4 famed Chicago musicians
entries.summary: <p>Imani and Searocket’s four hatchlings got names and bands — no, not that kind — to celebrate two weeks of life on Lake Michigan’s shore.</p><p>The four fuzzy, (and currently) flightless birds are now named Buddy, Frankie, Mavis and Tweedy after famed Chicago musicians Buddy Guy, Frankie Knuckles, Mavis Staples and Jeff Tweedy.</p><p>The Chicago Piping Plovers group said it received more than 456 submissions and more than 1,500 unique names for the chicks. A seven-person panel with representatives from various local city and conservation groups narrowed the list down.</p><p>“It seems fitting to name the chicks after musicians, as the scientific name of the Piping Plover is Charadrius melodus, referring to their melodious singing,” the Chicago Piping Plovers group said in a statement. “The artists selected span generations of fans through multiple genres, and have moved the arc of music forward with their innovation and talent, becoming Chicago and worldwide icons.”</p><p>They aren’t the first names based on the birds’ singing abilities, as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/environment/2024/07/20/piping-plover-chick-born-at-montrose-beach-ojibwe-name-nagamo" target="_blank" ><u>Nagamo</u></a>’s name was the Ojibwe phrase meaning “they sing.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <blockquote class="bluesky-embed" data-bluesky-uri="at://did:plc:k33a6y5zoxkzmhobrj4hczls/app.bsky.feed.post/3mpgf4ealys2j" data-bluesky-cid="bafyreidvpqvs5sqqzt62vbkwojckn2js4ek755i5pa6dftvwiapf4rvbhe"><p lang="en">Meet Buddy, Frankie, Mavis, and Tweedy! Today, each of your 2026 Chicago Piping Plover chicks received their unique leg bands and along with them their name. Here are the names and leg band combinations. 1/3</p>— <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:k33a6y5zoxkzmhobrj4hczls?ref_src=embed">Chicago Piping Plovers (@chicagopiping.bsky.social)</a> <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:k33a6y5zoxkzmhobrj4hczls/post/3mpgf4ealys2j?ref_src=embed">2026-06-29T11:29:14.455Z</a></blockquote><script async src="https://embed.bsky.app/static/embed.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div></div><p>Members of the Great Lakes Piping Plover Conservation Team, the Chicago Park District, Illinois Department of Natural Resources, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Chicago Piping Plovers helped put bands on the chicks to help track their growth. Typically, Great Lakes plovers have colored dots on their bands, though Chicago’s quartet have stars instead to match the city's flag.</p><p>It’s part of a 100-year-old U.S. Geological Survey program to track birds, according to the group.</p><p>To show they are Imani and Searocket’s hatchlings, the birds will all have a metal band on the upper left leg, an orange band on the lower left leg and a violet band on the lower right leg. The orange band will have distinct markers: Buddy bears a blue star, Frankie a red one, Mavis has yellow and Tweedy has green.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/06/21/piping-plover-chicks-imani-sea-rocket-montrose-beach-chicago" target="_blank" ><u>next major milestone</u></a> for the hatchlings will be around July 8, which is when the group considers them fully fledged whether or not they have actually begun to fly.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/06/21/piping-plover-chicks-imani-sea-rocket-montrose-beach-chicago" >For Father’s Day, Imani gets healthy week-old piping plover chicks</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/06/16/plover-chicks-hatch-montrose-beach" >4 plover chicks hatch at Montrose Beach</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.summary: <p>Ricardo Jiménez, director de iniciativas de salud pública del Centro Cultural Puertorriqueño, tiene toda la razón para guardar silencio.</p><p>Su activismo por la independencia de Puerto Rico le valió una condena a 90 años por alegaciones de conspiración sediciosa. Le fue concedido un indulto en 1999 por el presidente Bill Clinton y ha ayudado a dirigir el programa Vida/SIDA del Centro Cultural Puertorriqueño como un <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/04/01/aumentan-las-infecciones-por-vih-y-sida-en-chicago-tras-anos-de-disminucion-especialmente-entre-latinoshttps://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2026/04/01/aumentan-las-infecciones-por-vih-y-sida-en-chicago-tras-anos-de-disminucion-especialmente-entre-latinos" target="_blank" >consejero de VIH/SIDA</a> durante los últimos 15 años.</p><p>El domingo, él y otros del Centro Cultural Puertorriqueño encabezaron el 55.º desfile anual del Orgullo en Con 155 participantes, fue cuatro carrozas más largo que <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz/2025/06/30/habitantes-de-chicago-hacen-colorida-exhibicion-en-54%C2%BA-desfile-del-orgullo-sin-miedo" target="_blank" >el año pasado</a>.</p><p>El Centro Cultural Puertorriqueño, ubicado en Ukrainian Village, fue el líder destacado del desfile, que se utiliza para mostrar a grupos locales que trabajan para salvaguardar a la comunidad LGBTQ+, por su labor de “desmantelar la homofobia y la transfobia mientras integran la defensa LGBTQ+ en el núcleo de la salud pública y la justicia en vivienda”, según los organizadores del desfile.</p><p>El tema de este año, “Libre para ser orgulloso”, surge en medio de crecientes ataques contra la comunidad LGBTQ+ en todo el país, incluido Illinois, considerado en gran medida <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lgbtq/2025/03/12/trans-people-facing-gender-affirming-care-bans-flee-to-illinois-shield-law-states" target="_blank" >un refugio para las personas queer</a> en el Medio Oeste.</p><p>Jiménez dijo que, en medio de los ataques en curso contra la comunidad queer y los recortes a la financiación del tratamiento del VIH, era hora de que la comunidad queer tomara lecciones del activismo de antaño.</p><p>“Podríamos tener que protestar de nuevo para preservar nuestros derechos humanos”, dijo Jiménez, haciendo referencia al grupo de activistas queer de décadas atrás. “Venimos aquí unidos para asegurarnos de que lo ocurrido antes no vuelva a suceder”.</p><p>Antes de marchar en el desfile, el gobernador de Illinois, JB Pritzker, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/06/01/state-lawmakers-laud-passage-of-bills-protecting-reproductive-gender-affirming-care" target="_blank" >firmó tres leyes</a> destinadas a proteger a la comunidad LGBTQ+, incluyendo una que exige que las compañías de seguros en Illinois proporcionen al menos seis meses de medicamentos a los pacientes a quienes se les recetan hormonas y que elimine la entries.title: More Cubs injuries as Matt Shaw hits IL with sprained hand, interrupting utility man’s solid stretch at plate
entries.summary: <p>“We have a couple more injuries today, unfortunately,” <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> skipper <b>Craig Counsell</b> said to start his pregame media session Monday at Wrigley Field.</p><p>You know it’s bad when nobody even has to ask.</p><p>Yes, there’s more bad injury news for the Cubs, who couldn’t make it consecutive days without sending a player to the injured list.</p><p>Monday, it was a pair, with utility man <b>Matt Shaw</b> landing on the IL with a sprained left hand and righty reliever <b>Ethan Roberts</b> heading there with inflammation in his right forearm.</p><p>That made six injured-list placements in six days.</p><p>Though Roberts’ presence in an increasingly injury-ravaged bullpen is a much needed one, Shaw was on something of a hot streak since returning from his previous IL stint earlier this month.</p><p>He had a .395 on-base percentage in 14 games in June, seeing regular playing time as the team’s primary right fielder while <b>Seiya Suzuki</b> has battled nagging knee discomfort that’s limited him to DH duty. Among Cubs hitters, only Suzuki and the red-hot <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b> had a higher June OPS than Shaw’s .852 coming into Monday.</p><p>But the Cubs don’t seem concerned that Shaw will be sidelined long.</p><p>“We’re pretty optimistic here,” Counsell said. “We ruled out everything else that could have been longer term, in terms of worrisome. He’s got some pretty good swelling in there right now, and we’ve got to get rid of that. But I think there’s a world where he’s swinging a bat by the weekend.</p><p>“As soon as we get the inflammation out, we think we can move forward pretty quickly. There’s a chance that one’s a minimum [stay].”</p><h3><b>On the pitching side … </b></h3><h3></h3><p>Things are much more dire when it comes to the Cubs’ collection of arms, where they’re facing an outrageous amount of concurrent injuries.</p><p>Roberts has been among the several heavily used pitchers in a bullpen that’s down closer <b>Daniel Palencia</b> and lost late-inning men <b>Phil Maton</b> and <b>Hoby Milner</b> in the last week.</p><p>The results weren’t good during his 11 appearances this month — he has an 8.38 June ERA — culminating in Sunday’s struggle of an outing in the 10th inning against the Brewers, when he faced three batters, giving up a couple hits and a walk, charged with both runs scored in that frame.</p><p>But with the Cubs facing a shortage of healthy arms, losing Roberts, even with those results, is not ideal.</p><p>“Ethan’s been one of the guys that’s pitched a lot,” Counsell said. “I don’t think we have anything serious here. We’ve got to give him a break, basically. But he’s got some symptoms, yeah.”</p><h3><b>Up from the minors</b></h3><h3></h3><p>To take the spots vacated by Shaw and Roberts, the Cubs brought outfielder <b>Kevin Alcantara</b> and relief pitcher <b>Gavin Hollowell</b> up from Triple-A.</p><p>We’ll see if and how Alcantara factors into the plans in right field with Shaw sidelined.</p><p>The Cubs started <b>Michael Conforto</b> in right for Monday’s series-opener against the Padres. Conforto, though, has only received four plate appearances against left-handed pitchers this season.</p><p>“Matt was doing a good job,” Counsell said. “It now falls on somebody else to pick up the slack. Michael Conforto’s going to get more regular at-bats, that’s kind of the logical thing here.</p><p>“Against lefties, we’re going to have to figure out how we want to move guys around.”</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-hide-descriptions="true" entries.title: Alex Bregman stays under microscope, sparking Cubs fan frustration after failing to beat out bobbled grounder
entries.summary: <p>Alex Bregman wishes he would have run a little harder Sunday in Milwaukee.</p><p>Thanks to a bobble, a seemingly routine ground out to shortstop turned into a chance for a base runner on a day where runs were at a premium against an effective Brewers pitching staff.</p><p>But Bregman, far from busting it down the first-base line, couldn’t take advantage and was thrown out, much to the dismay of fans already frustrated with a lack of offensive results from the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ big-ticket free agent.</p><p>The play even earned something of an admonishment from Cubs announcer Jim Deshaies.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Alex Bregman hasn’t been a Cub for more than a cup of coffee, but he’s already wearing out his welcome.<br><br>The $175 million man heard it from the Cubs broadcast team on Sunday for not hustling down the line. <br><br>Read more: <a href="https://t.co/0BZ46ddg6l">https://t.co/0BZ46ddg6l</a> <a href="https://t.co/3ozUM86wIM">pic.twitter.com/3ozUM86wIM</a></p>— New York Post Sports (@nypostsports) <a href="https://x.com/nypostsports/status/2071611253957480462?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">June 29, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>“Yes,” the third baseman said, asked Monday if he regretted not running harder, before adding some context. “And I’ve also had 10 soft-tissue injuries running down the first-base line, specifically.</p><p>“There’s kind of some give and take. But at the same time, obviously, I wish I beat the throw.”</p><p>Experienced hands like Bregman know their bodies, and there is a balance between going hard enough to make something happen and overdoing it to the point of risking injury.</p><p>But Sunday’s mistake proved a bad look for a player who’s been slow to show, statistically, why the Cubs shelled out $175 million for his services last winter.</p><p>Blunt in answers about how his season has gone to this point, Bregman is the last person who needs to be reminded of his lack of production. He’s a studious presence in the clubhouse with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/12/cubs-alex-bregman-offense-free-agent-contract-carson-kelly-matthew-boyd-injury-craig-counsell" >a reputation of being among the hardest workers around</a>.</p><p>But that reputation has yet to equal results, and he came into Monday still searching, the owner of a .335 slugging percentage that ranked in the bottom 15 of qualified hitters in baseball. His .671 OPS would be the lowest of his career by a wide margin, the previous low-water mark .768 two seasons ago.</p><p>His .181 batting average and .253 slugging percentage in June were particularly ugly.</p><p>Obviously, he’s working to try to fix it. What’s he working on, exactly?</p><p>“What’s your guess?” he responded jokingly, acknowledging his struggles have been obvious to anyone watching. “Hitting the baseball.”</p><p>Asked to get more specific, the answer remained easily predictable. The guy with a career slugging percentage .135 points higher than his current number is trying to hit for more power.</p><p>“Just being in a consistent spot to be able to hit the ball hard in the air,” he said. “Get back to swinging at pitches that I want to hit and not swinging at pitches that are outside the strike zone. Basically the same stuff. Hit the ball, swing at pitches I can drive and take pitches that I can’t. Hone it in, be better.”</p><p>Plenty of frustrated fans would agree that “be better” is a good target.</p><p>The Cubs, with their big-money investment in the two-time World Series champ, are unsurprisingly expecting “better” to show up any day now.</p><p>Could a loud turnaround moment – like the 15 RBIs previously slumping shortstop Dansby Swanson, the team’s second highest paid player, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/24/cubs-dansby-swanson-grand-slam-two-homers-seven-rbis-pete-crow-armstrong-craig-counsell-offense-mets-doubleheader" >racked up in two days against the Mets</a> — be on the horizon for Bregman?</p><p>“He works and works and works,” team president Jed Hoyer said last week in New York. “No one’s going to outwork him to figure out what it is [that’s wrong].</p><p>“I was getting peppered with questions on the radio the other day about Dansby and his struggles. All of a sudden — ‘snap’ — he breaks out of it. That’s how it happens.</p><p>“My expectation is at some point, [Alex] will get red hot, and these questions will be a distant memory. In the meantime, he’s trying to get on base, he’s getting some hits, but the slug just hasn’t been there. It’s kind of always been there for him, and I’m sure it’s a matter of time before we see that.”</p><p>If the Cubs can get that out of Bregman, it’s another massive boost to an offense recently revived from an early-summer slumber, and it would be extraordinarily helpful in bailing out an injury-ravaged pitching staff.</p><p>Until such a turnaround comes, though, Bregman will stay under the microscope of Cubs fans waiting for him to play up to the contract that got them so excited in the offseason.</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 entries.title: Altgeld Gardens' 'Up Top' building to return to tip-top shape as an after-school center
entries.summary: <p>A $23.3 million effort to turn an architecturally significant 81-year-old former Altgeld Gardens commercial building into an after-school center has been approved by the Chicago Plan Commission.</p><p>The panel last week approved By The Hand Club For Kids' project to convert and expand the dilapidated one-story modernist building, 13100 S. Ellis Ave., into a facility with classrooms, a gymnasium and meeting space.</p><p>The development represents quite a potential turnaround for one of the city's less recognized but historically important buildings.</p><p>Designed by noted modernist architects Keck & Keck — and nicknamed the "Up Top" building by Altgeld residents — the distinctive fan-shaped brick structure with an overhanging curved roof was built in 1945 as stores, offices and services for the then-new Far South Side public housing development.</p><p>The building became the birthplace of the environmental justice movement in the 1980s when the late Altgeld resident Hazel Johnson's People for Community Recovery set up shop there.</p><p>The Up Top was granted preliminary city landmark status earlier this month.</p><p>"We just think that there's so much great history in the building, and we know it's something the community wanted us to do," By The Hand Club For Kids Chief of Partnerships and Development Andraya Yousfi said. "Lots of incredible history in the building that's really meaningful for the community."</p><p>By The Hand Club has been active at Altgeld for 25 years. The housing development's Local Advisory Council President Bernadette Williams was instrumental in getting the organization to reuse the building.</p><p>"With them preserving it, it's going to be a new amenity [that helps with the] beautification of Altgeld Gardens," Williams said. "It's an eyesore right now."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-6e0000" entries.title: Seranthony Dominguez loses closer role — for now — in fluid White Sox bullpen
entries.summary: <p>BALTIMORE — The titles and roles have been fluid in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a> manager Will Venable’s bullpen.</p><p>He named Seranthony Dominguez his closer in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/02/13/white-sox-bullpen-spring-training-seranthony-dominguez-jordan-hicks" target="_blank" ><u>spring training</u></a>, in case the right-hander’s two-year, $20 million free-agent signing didn’t announce that itself.</p><p>But all season, Venable has <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/06/15/chicago-white-sox-bullpen-closer-seranthony-dominguez-bryan-hudson-will-venable-zach-bove-sean-newcomb-grant-taylor-braves-dodgers" >played the matchups</a> in high-leverage situations regardless of the inning or save opportunity, often turning to flame-throwing reliever Grant Taylor in the biggest moments but also showing faith in lanky southern Illinois native Bryan Hudson.</p><p>Now, after a tough month for Dominguez with a pair of blown saves against division rivals, Venable is taking the Sox’ big-money reliever out of the late-game equation — for now, at least.</p><p>The 31-year-old veteran, who played in the World Series last season for the Blue Jays, pitched a scoreless sixth inning in Sunday’s loss to the Royals, the earliest he’d entered a game this season.</p><p>Venable called it “a little bit of a lower leverage spot to get him back on line, and obviously he did a great job.”</p><p>“It’s just a little bump in the road, but we are not worried about titles or changing roles,” Venable said. “It’s about getting him in a good spot and getting him back on line.”</p><p>The second-year manager told Dominguez last week that he’d be seeing earlier action in lower-pressure situations to get back on track, after Dominguez blew his fourth and fifth saves of the season on consecutive days against the Tigers and Guardians.</p><p>The first outing of his reset went well enough, with Dominguez giving up a single and striking out two, including All-Star shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. to end the frame.</p><p>“It made me feel good, because the things that I've been working on got a good result,” said Dominguez, who is taking the demotion, however temporary, in stride.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> entries.title: Supreme Court rejects GOP mail ballot challenge, but Illinois Dems warn voting rights 'still under attack'
entries.summary: <p>Top Democrats in Illinois are applauding the U.S. Supreme Court's ruling on Monday that will allow the state to continue to count mail-in ballots that are postmarked by Election Day. </p><p>The challenge, backed by President Donald Trump and led by the Republican National Committee, is the latest in the president's efforts to block mail-in ballots, which he has tried to link to voter fraud. Trump is also still pushing for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would ban mail ballots and also require voters to present proof of citizenship with a passport or birth certificate when they register to vote.</p><p>Federal law already requires that voters in federal elections be U.S. citizens — and there is little evidence to suggest those who lack legal status are trying to vote. </p><p>The 5-4 Supreme Court decision targeted laws in 14 states and the District of Columbia, including Illinois, which permits mailed ballots to arrive and be counted for several days after an election if they are postmarked by Election Day. There are 36 states that require absentee or mail ballots to be received on or before Election Day. The ruling is a big loss for Trump — but spares election officials from huge complications ahead of the November midterm elections. </p><p>Justice Amy Coney Barrett wrote the court's majority opinion, joined by Chief Justice John Roberts and the three liberal justices. </p><p>Federal laws setting a single Election Day "leave open when those votes must be received," Barrett wrote in the opinion. </p><p>In a Truth Social post, Trump called the ruling a "tremendous loss" and urged Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, which would require voters to show photo identification, proof of citizenship and ban mail-in ballots except for illness, disability, military deployment or travel.</p><p>"There is no excuse for a politician, or otherwise, to be against the above three requirements," Trump wrote. "There is only one reason to oppose — CHEATING!"</p><p>According to the Illinois State Board of Elections, voters can apply for a mail ballot up to five days before an election, although election officials urge voters to consider applying for a ballot as early as possible. Ballots sent through the U.S. Postal Service must be postmarked on or before Election Day. Illinois allows ballots to be counted for up to two weeks after Election Day, as long as they are postmarked appropriately. </p><p>Voters can mail their ballots, deliver them in person to the local election authority office, or in many election jurisdictions drop them in a secure drop box. Completed ballots are not accepted at polling places or early voting locations. And voters trying to do so are instead offered the option of surrendering their mail ballot and voting in person instead.</p><p>In Illinois, any voter who registers for the first time or has address change must bring two forms of ID to vote, one of which shows their current address. Although ID requirements vary at different locations, election authorities recommend bringing at least one form of identification in case there are any questions. </p><p>Top Illinois Democrats like Gov. JB Pritzker and Sen. Dick Durbin praised the ruling — but both are warning that Trump's attacks on voting rights aren't over. </p><p>Pritzker said in a statement that Trump is using "every weapon in his arsenal to attack our free and fair elections." </p><p>"The Supreme Court ruled against him today on an asinine attempt to throw out a law that ensures mail ballots get counted, but his assault is not over," the governor said. "We cannot look away while the most corrupt president in history attempts to rewrite our election laws to serve his own interests.”</p><p> Durbin called the ruling a "victory," but warned, "voting rights are still under attack." He is urging Congress to pass the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, which would update and restore safeguards of the original Voting Rights Act. The measure addresses voter suppression and would ensure every voter, regardless of race or background, would have equal access to the ballot box. </p><p>The Supreme Court in April ruled that Louisiana's 2024 congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, essentially weakening an argument plaintiffs have used to protect against racial discrimination in voting and representation. </p><p> "To preserve the right to vote for every eligible American," Durbin said in a statement, "Congress must take action to protect this precious right, including passing the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore and strengthen the protections of the Voting Rights Act.”</p>

entries.title: Lake County judge denies Marni Yang's bid for new trial
entries.summary: <p>A Lake County judge has denied Marni Yang’s bid for a new trial in the 2007 murder of a 42-year-old pregnant woman whom authorities say she saw as a rival for the affections of former Chicago Bear Shaun Gayle, according to court documents.</p><p>Lake County Judge Christopher Stride ruled Monday the defense's claims of Yang's innocence were insufficient to overrule the evidence that she was guilty.</p><p>Lake County State's Attorney Eric Rinehart said the office "agreed" with the court's decision.</p><p>"More importantly, we are relieved for the family that we are getting closer to finality in this case," Rinehart said. "We continue to keep Rhoni and her loved ones in our thoughts.”</p><p>Yang was convicted of first-degree murder charges in 2011 for the killing of Rhoni Reuter, who was found shot dead in her Deerfield home Oct. 4, 2007. Yang later received two life sentences for the deaths of Reuter and her unborn child.</p><p>In January, former Oak Park police officer and forensic expert Arthur Borchers <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/01/13/experts-say-marni-yang-could-not-have-killed-romantic-rival-unborn-child-in-2007" >testified</a> that Yang could not have killed Reuter. Her attorneys previously pointed to DNA from an unknown man on five unspent bullet shells found at the crime scene and a report stating the killer was taller than Yang as exonerating evidence.</p><p>Previously, defense expert Dr. Cyril H. Wecht — an attorney and forensic pathologist who has performed more than 21,000 autopsies — testified that blunt-force injuries on Reuter’s face, including a black left eye and scrapes around her lips and chin, happened days before she was killed. Her defense has also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/1/22/21077433/marni-yang-defense-checking-shaun-gayles-alibi" >questioned Gayle’s alibi</a>.</p><p>Yang's attorney, Jed Stone, said he was "disappointed" and that she questioned the ruling.</p><p>He began the process of appealing the decision Monday. If that appeal fails, he plans to go to the state Supreme Court, and federal court after that.</p><p>“We’re not done,” said Stone, 77. "We will keep on fighting."</p>

entries.title: Bally's raises eyebrows by hiring ex-Mayor Lightfoot's law firm to challenge video gambling terminals
entries.summary: <p>Bally’s has hired former Mayor Lori Lightfoot's law firm to help potentially sue Chicago for violating the casino host agreement that she negotiated as mayor — a suit that would be based on the city’s decision to legalize video gambling terminals.</p><p>“We are pleased to have built an excellent and knowledgeable team here in Chicago. As we ramp up efforts to protect our investment in the city, we have also brought on the strategic counsel of RKF Global PLLC, where former Mayor Lightfoot is a partner,” Bally’s said in a statement.</p><p>Lightfoot refused to comment on her surprise involvement in Bally’s long-threatened legal challenge, which was first disclosed by Crain’s Chicago Business.</p><p>The $16.6 billion 2026 budget <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/12/23/mayor-brandon-johnson-city-council-alternate-budget" target="_blank" >approved by a City Council </a>majority lifted the Chicago ban on video gambling and assumed Chicago would generate $6.8 million by licensing newly legalized <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/09/16/video-gaming-in-chicago-proposal-anthony-beale-brandon-johnson" target="_blank" >video gambling terminals</a> across the city. Bally's, which is building a permanent casino in the River West neighborhood, strongly opposes legalized video gambling in the city.</p><p></p><p>David Greising, president and CEO of the Better Government Association, branded Lightfoot’s involvement "a pretty bald conflict of interest." His reading of the city's ethics ordinance is that the former mayor "can't assist an employer or client on a contract over which they had substantial managerial responsibility for the life of that contract."</p><p>“She is being hired to represent a client challenging their allegations about an agreement that she negotiated when she was mayor. It just feels like she’s playing on both sides here,” Greising said.</p><p>Greising noted that there was "was a lot of complaining at the time" Lightfoot <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2022/5/25/23141244/ballys-casino-approved-chicago-city-council-river-west-medinah-temple-lightfoot-police-fire-pensions" >made her choice</a> that "Bally’s had the inside track and that she had her thumb on the scale — that she favored them as a bidder."</p><p>“I don’t think there was any hard and fast proof of that. But it still does raise questions about the objectivity of the process way back then," Greising said. “This company has been in trouble right from the get-go. We’ve seen how it has affected the slow-motion development of that property. There is good reason to question the choice and this just raises more questions about her relationship to Bally’s.”</p><p>Ald. Anthony Beale (9th), the City Council’s chief proponent of video gambling terminals, condemned Bally’s decision to hire Lightfoot to represent the company.</p><p>“That is a quid pro quo to try to reward somebody who gave them a contract that they never should have gotten in the first place,” Beale said. “Their credit rating was bad. They had never built a casino They’re one of the lowest-performing operators out there. And they were the only ones to commit to giving her $40 million to plug her budget hole.”</p><p>Steven Berlin, executive director of the Chicago Board of Ethics, said he couldn’t comment on Bally’s decision, but added that generally, the city’s ethics ordinance bars a former mayor — for a year after leaving office — from “assisting or representing a new client in subject matters they were personally and substantially involved in.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2023/2/3/23581737/lori-lightfoot-ballys-casino-latoyia-huggins-michael-mackey-chicago-community-builders-collective" >These are some of the people in line to profit from Lightfoot’s Bally’s casino deal</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Three years ago, Lightfoot convinced the City Council to ratify her choice of Bally’s to secure $40 million in upfront payments from Bally’s to keep police and fire pensions solvent and stave off a pre-election property tax increase.</p><p>At the time, Ald. Brian Hopkins (2nd) and Ald. Brendan Reilly (42nd) tried and failed to convince their colleagues to reject Bally’s bid. They argued that the $1.7 billion permanent casino and entertainment complex in River West would create an impossible bottleneck in an already congested area, and that Bally's has never built a casino from the ground up.</p><p>They also accused Lightfoot of going around the City Council committee she created to give herself "political cover" for a decision she had already made. </p><p>Reilly added that Lightfoot's 11th-hour "switcheroo" to the landmark Medinah Temple as the site for Bally's temporary casino would make an alarming spike in River North crime worse, and that the already congested area could not handle the influx of traffic.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/12/23/mayor-brandon-johnson-city-council-alternate-budget" target="_blank" ></a><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/09/16/video-gaming-in-chicago-proposal-anthony-beale-brandon-johnson" target="_blank" ></a></p><p></p><p>The decision to lift the Chicago ban on video gambling terminals has divided the City Council and exacerbated tensions between alderpersons and Mayor Brandon Johnson.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2025/10/09/ballys-casino-anthony-beale-video-gambling-proposal-chicago-lost-revenue" >Bally’s has warned</a> that lifting Chicago’s ban on video gambling would cost the cash-strapped city $74 million in annual revenue and up to 1,050 jobs at its temporary and permanent casinos.</p><p>The casino giant has further warned that lifting the long-standing Chicago ban would force the Johnson administration to renegotiate “critical elements” of its host agreement, wipe out a yearly $4 million lump-sum payment from Bally’s and shrink the casino jackpot needed to save police and fire pension funds.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/06/11/mayor-brandon-johnson-repeal-video-gambling-bid-chicago" >Johnson has raised</a> strong objections to legalizing video gambling, in part because he believes it would violate the city’s host agreement with Bally’s and expose the city to a lawsuit filed by the casino giant.</p><p></p>

entries.title: Stacey King honored by Bulls in Celebration of Life ceremony on Monday
entries.summary: <p>The Bulls honored three-time NBA Champion and television broadcaster Stacey King with a Celebration of Life ceremony at the Advocate Center on Monday, with speakers that included Bulls CEO and President Michael Reinsdorf, King’s former broadcast teammates Neil Funk and Adam Amin, and his sons Erick, Garrett and Brandon King.</p><p>King died earlier this month after 19 years behind the microphone for the franchise, and his impact both on and off the court was best summed up by Michael Reinsdorf.</p><p>“Over the last three decades, Stacey became so much more than just a former player or our television analyst,” Reinsdorf said. “He became one of the defining personalities of Chicago Bulls basketball. He meant so much to me, to my family, to my dad (Jerry Reinsdorf), who is here today, to everyone in our organization, to the city of Chicago, and to Bulls fans all over the world. He was clearly one of one. Incredibly talented, hilarious, authentic, there simply won’t be another Stacey.”</p><p>As far as how the team plans to honor King for the upcoming season, that was yet to be announced but it will undoubtedly match King’s personality and be big.</p><p>There has also been no movement on a replacement for King just yet, but that could also start to move forward in the upcoming months.</p><p>King, 59, was a member of the first three Bulls’ championships from 1991-93 after being a standout force at Oklahoma. In eight NBA seasons, he also played with Minnesota, Miami, Boston and Dallas, averaging 6.4 points and 3.3 rebounds.</p><p>The sixth overall pick in 1989, King played in all 82 games as a rookie, coming off the bench and averaging 8.9 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.</p>

entries.title: Blackhawks give qualifying offers to four RFAs including Connor Bedard
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks?_gl=1*4snu0o*_up*MQ..*_ga*NzA2MDU1Mjg1LjE3ODI3NjE1MDc.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODI3NjE1MDYkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODI3NjE1MTEkajU1JGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> had straightforward decisions to make with their restricted free agents this year, and they made the expected ones.</p><p>Four RFAs — forward Connor Bedard, defensemen Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro and goalie Drew Commesso — were all given qualifying offers before the Monday deadline, allowing the Hawks to retain their rights past the expiration of their entry-level contracts Wednesday.</p><p>The only two RFAs not given qualifying offers were AHL defensemen Dmitri Kuzmin and Ryan Mast, neither of whom were NHL-relevant prospects. Kuzmin is rumored to be signing in the KHL.</p><p>Bedard headlines the group of qualified RFAs, but only Commesso holds arbitration rights within the group.</p><p>Contract negotiations between the Hawks and Bedard's agents have <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/06/23/connor-bedard-blackhawks-contract-negotiations-nhl-free-agency-leo-carlsson-adam-fantilli?_gl=1*1l9umti*_up*MQ..*_ga*NzA2MDU1Mjg1LjE3ODI3NjE1MDc.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODI3NjE1MDYkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODI3NjE1MDYkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >revved up recently</a>, with the two sides exchanging numbers and working toward an agreement.</p><p>It's still unknown what length of contract Bedard will eventually sign and for what annual salary-cap hit (likely within the $13-16 million range), but fans need not worry about the possibility of him signing an offer sheet with another team. That's an unrealistic idea.</p><p>Korchinski, Del Mastro and Commesso will likely receive one- or two-year contracts with low cap hits, extending their windows to establish themselves as NHL players without guaranteeing long-term commitments in case they don't.</p><p>The two defensemen are no longer waiver-exempt next season, so training camp will be crucial for them. Korchinski hopes his summer of training in Chicago prepares him well for a potentially make-or-break season.</p>
entries.author: Ben Pope

entries.title: Mayor Johnson's renter protection proposal faces fierce resistance from building owners
entries.summary: <p>If Mayor Brandon Johnson hopes to confront Chicago’s affordability crisis by leveling the playing field between renters and landlords, he’ll have to defeat the same real estate interests that shot down his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2024/03/19/bring-chicago-home-election-referendum-results" >Bring Chicago Home referendum.</a></p><p>That much was obvious Monday after Johnson introduced his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/05/29/mayor-brandon-johnson-ordinance-protects-chicago-renters-housing" >“Protecting Renters Ordinance,” </a>and the Housing Committee chaired by one of his closest City Council allies — progressive firebrand Ald. Byron Sigcho-Lopez (25th) — held its first public hearing on the mayor’s ordinance.</p><p>“The resistance we face will be fierce. Corporate interests are already organizing to preserve the status quo. But we will not back down,” Johnson said Monday before the hearing. </p><p>Landlords showed up in force to protest an ordinance that would ban move-in fees and other "junk fees" without a documented cost, offer legal representation for income-eligible tenants and require landlords to provide a $10,000 payment or 10 months' rent — whichever is greater — to tenants evicted or not renewed without “just cause.”</p><p>“It’s going to become stricter and stricter for the housing provider to approve that tenant because they have to renew their lease forever," one landlord told the committee.</p><p>Another point of contention is the proposed annual registration fee of $20 per unit to generate $20 million a year for inspections, attorneys and other enforcement costs. That fee is part of a provision within the ordinance that would establish a rental registry to log of who owns the city's more than 500,000 rental units, and whether those landlords are complying with the law. That measure was included in Johnson's proposal in reaction to a WBEZ/Chicago Sun-Times story about how landlords often set up limited liability companies to mask who they are — creating an anonymity that makes it hard to hold problem landlords accountable.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2025/09/05/chicago-landlords-renters-property-management-llc" >Chicago’s invisible property owners</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>The mayor’s original version would have required $10,000 in compensation to tenants who chose to move out to avoid “unconscionable rent increases.”</p><p>But that provision has been removed amid complaints that it could be a dangerous first step toward rent control, which would require a change in state law. A proposal that building owners provide interest on security deposits has also been dropped.</p><p>The changes were not enough to satisfy building owners.</p><p>“Costs this large do not simply disappear. They are absorbed into the rental market through higher rents, deferred maintenance and fewer available units,” said Miguel Chacon, policy committee vice chair for the Chicago Association of Realtors. “Chicago’s housing crisis will not be solved by making rental housing harder to provide, which is what this ordinance does.”</p><p>Edgewater community activist John Holden, who owns several small residential buildings, warned that “piling on” landlords at a time when property taxes, insurance and utility costs are soaring might be the “straw that breaks the camel’s back.”</p><p></p><p>“If we start driving out all the small mom-and-pop landlords and everything falls into the hands of corporate landlords," Holden said, "we’re really going to have a housing problem in this city. Please don’t make life much worse for small landlords.”</p><p>Johnson’s policy chief, Jung Yoon, said the relocation assistance required of mom-and-pop landlords has been reduced “in an understanding of the different types of burdens” building owners face.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" And it was enraging to see people bringing all of these concerns to our office over and over and over and not having a way to hold this landlord accountable."</p><p>Ald. Anthony Quezada (35th) said building housing and strengthening renters' protections "are not competing goals. They go hand in hand."</p><p>Zoning Committee Chair Gilbert Villegas (36th) said building owners are “in the business to make money" and they will almost certainly "pass this on to the renter.” </p><p>"I know you want to get this going. But if we can have further discussions on how to make this a little bit better so, that way, some of us can support it, I would appreciate it," Villegas said.</p><p>Finance Chair Pat Dowell (3rd) noted that direct introductions to committee are supposed to be limited to emergencies and “this does not seem to be an emergency.”</p><p>When Yoon said top mayoral aides have “heard plenty of stories from tenants who can’t afford to wait,” Dowell said, “That’s a bunch of junk.”</p>
